title: Cache entropy impact mapping — microburst & cold-start scenarios
content:
Overview:
This working doc explores how user/session "entropy" (degree of prefix diversity) affects prefix/KV cache hit rates during three operational regimes: steady-state, microbursts (short high-QPS spikes), and rolling cold-starts (new model versions or shard restarts). Goal is to produce a small spreadsheet-ready mapping that product/infra can use to estimate token-level savings and recommend conservative prefetch/TTL policies.

Key definitions & assumptions (for modelling):
- Entropy: a proxy metric for per-customer prefix diversity. Low entropy => repeated prefixes; high entropy => many unique prefixes.
- Prefix similarity: fraction of requests that share a cacheable prefix with at least one prior request in the lookback window.
- Lookback window: time horizon for KV/prefix cache effectiveness (configurable: 30s / 5m / 30m).
- Baseline token unit cost: $0.0008 per input+output token (hosted rate for reference workload).
- Avg tokens per request: 60 tokens (input+output combined) unless stated otherwise.
- Warmup/prefetch cost: prefetching a prefix costs ~1 request worth of tokens (approx 60 tokens). We assume prefetches are triggered only for prefixes expected to save > prefetch cost.

Quick modelling notes (spreadsheet-ready):
- Use these columns: Scenario, EntropyIndex (0..1), LookbackSec, PrefixSimilarityPct, PredictedKVHitPct, AvgTokensPerReq, RequestsPerMillion, TokensServedPerM, TokenSavingsPerM, CostReductionPct, Notes

Sample rows (CSV style — paste into sheet):
Scenario,EntropyIndex,LookbackSec,PrefixSimilarityPct,PredictedKVHitPct,AvgTokensPerReq,RequestsPerMillion,TokensServedPerM,TokenSavingsPerM,CostReductionPct,Notes
steady-low-entropy,0.15,300,32,22,60,1000000,60000000,13200000,17.6,"Low diversity product region; expected good cacheability; steady traffic"
steady-high-entropy,0.85,300,6,4,60,1000000,60000000,2400000,3.2,"High variety queries (Q&A aggregator); minimal prefix reuse"
microburst-low-entropy,0.20,30,40,30,60,500000,30000000,9000000,13.5,"Short spike where sessions repeat (e.g., flash sale bot traffic)"
microburst-high-entropy,0.80,30,8,6,60,500000,30000000,1800000,3.6,"Burst of many unique requests; cache cold; small benefit"
coldstart-rolling,0.45,1800,12,9,60,200000,12000000,1080000,4.5,"Rolling restarts where some shards warm slowly"
hybrid-prefetch,0.40,60,18,14,60,800000,48000000,6720000,10.5,"Aggressive prefetch for mid-entropy customers (prefetch cost accounted)"

How columns are computed (simple formulas to implement in sheet):
- TokensServedPerM = RequestsPerMillion * AvgTokensPerReq
- TokenSavingsPerM = TokensServedPerM * PredictedKVHitPct / 100
- CostReductionPct = (TokenSavingsPerM * unit_cost) / (TokensServedPerM * unit_cost) * 100 = PredictedKVHitPct
Notes: above assumes that a KV hit saves the full downstream token generation cost for the cached portion; in practice partial-prefix hits yield fractional savings.

Sensitivity experiments to run (recommended sheet tabs):
1) Entropy sweep: EntropyIndex from 0.05 to 0.95 step 0.05; lookback windows = [30s, 60s, 300s, 1800s]; plot predicted hit% and cost reduction.
2) Microburst short-window resilience: simulate 10x QPS for 30s with different warmup strategies (no warm, opportunistic prefix-warmers, proactive prefetch).
3) Prefetch cost amortization: evaluate minimum expected hit probability required for a prefetch to pay back within T seconds.
4) TTL / eviction policy tradeoffs: simulate LRU vs time-decay policies under mixed entropy traffic.

Small worked example (calculation trace):
- Scenario: hybrid-prefetch (row above). Prefetch policy warms top-50 prefixes per customer during session start at cost ~50*60 tokens = 3000 tokens if fully executed. If average session issues 30 requests and predicted hit% after warm is 40% across following requests, net savings estimate = (30 req * 60 tokens * 0.40) - 3000 = (720 * 0.4) - 3000 = 288 - 3000 = -2712 tokens => negative. So prefetch needs to be more selective (top-5 prefixes or triggered only after 5th request).

Operational recommendations (draft guidance):
- Conservative default: Lookback 300s, TTL adaptive by entropy bucket (low-entropy customers: TTL 1800s; mid-entropy: 300s; high-entropy: 60s).
- Microburst policy: enable short lookback layer (30s) with aggressive batching + admission control to avoid warming eviction storms. Use request-scoped prefix aggregation to avoid prefetching long tail during bursts.
- Prefetch guardrails: limit prefetch to top-N candidate prefixes OR only when predicted payoff > X tokens (configurable threshold). Start with N=5 and payoff threshold = 300 tokens.
- Monitoring: add per-customer entropy metric + rolling 1h hit-rate heatmap. Alert if hit-rate delta > 10pp following model rollouts.

Risks & open questions (items to experiment before production rollout):
- How correlated are prefix sequences within sessions for top 20% of customers? Need sample traces.
- Prefetch amortization depends heavily on average session length — expand sampling to 30, 60, 90 day windows.
- Cold-start due to model binary changes vs runtime process restarts: separate these events in trace annotations.

Next steps / immediate experiments (owners assigned):
- Data pull: infra-runner to export 7-days of prefix traces (anon) covering 5k top customers — Owner: Marcus Li — due 2025-06-25.
- Entropy sweep sim: single-node Monte Carlo that varies entropy and request arrival patterns — Owner: Evelyn Chen — due 2025-07-01.
- Prefetch pilot: implement selective prefetch (top-3 per-session only) in staging for 2 customers — Owner: Samir Rao — target start 2025-07-10.

Notes to self / TODOs:
- Add a sheet tab that converts TokenSavingsPerM into monthly $ savings for different pricing tiers (hosted vs dedicated).
- Cross-reference with 'routing and fallbacks' playbook to ensure warmers respect fallback policies.
- Sanity-check: run above small spreadsheet on both dev and prod sample traces to validate modeled hit% vs realized.

Appendix: quick heuristics table (for PMs/SEs):
- If observed per-customer prefix similarity > 20% and avg session length > 10, target prefetch conservative (top-3) => expect 8–12% token savings.
- If microburst detected (QPS x5 sustained > 15s) and prefix similarity > 30%, enable short-window lookback to capture burst reuse => expect 10–18% token savings for that window.
- High entropy & short sessions: focus on other optimizations (quantization, batching) instead of aggressive caching.

End of draft — feedback welcome.
